question.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(8,-6,5)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨-8,6,3⟩=24.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a point on the plane. If $r=⟨x,y,z⟩,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-8,6,3⟩ & =24 \\ -8x+6y+3z & =24 \\ 3z & =24+8x-6y \\ z & =8+\frac{8}{3}x-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $x=3$ and $y=1,$ we get 

$$
z=8+\frac{8}{3}(3)-2(1)=14.
$$

So, the point $Q(3,1,14)$ lies on the plane. 

Now, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨3,1,14⟩-⟨8,-6,5⟩ \\  & =⟨-5,7,9⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨-8,6,3⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-5)\cdot (-8)+7\cdot 6+9\cdot 3|}{\sqrt{(-8)^{2}+{6}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|40+42+27|}{\sqrt{64+36+9}} \\  & =\frac{|109|}{\sqrt{109}} \\  & =\sqrt{109}\end{aligned}
$$
